params.query:
WITH raw_flights AS (
  SELECT
    icao,
    r AS registration,
    aircraft_type,
    start_t,
    end_t,
    start_height_agl_ft,
    end_height_agl_ft,
    ST_MakeLine(list_transform(geometry, g -> ST_Point(g.x, g.y))) AS geom
  FROM read_parquet([
    'https://data.source.coop/root-geospatial/flight-tracks/quadkey_z8=02301200/year=2024/month=6/day=15/flights-2024-06-15.parquet',
    'https://data.source.coop/root-geospatial/flight-tracks/quadkey_z8=02301201/year=2024/month=6/day=15/flights-2024-06-15.parquet',
    'https://data.source.coop/root-geospatial/flight-tracks/quadkey_z8=02301210/year=2024/month=6/day=15/flights-2024-06-15.parquet',
    'https://data.source.coop/root-geospatial/flight-tracks/quadkey_z8=02301211/year=2024/month=6/day=15/flights-2024-06-15.parquet'
  ])
),
unique_flights AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (icao, end_t)
    icao,
    registration,
    aircraft_type,
    start_t,
    end_t,
    start_height_agl_ft,
    end_height_agl_ft,
    geom
  FROM raw_flights
  WHERE geom IS NOT NULL
)
-- Where each flight starts and ends, for the points drawn there
SELECT *, ST_StartPoint(geom) AS start_point, ST_EndPoint(geom) AS end_point
FROM unique_flights
LIMIT 500

inputs.text: This query loads up to 500 flight tracks over California's Central Coast on June 15, 2024, from an online dataset.
This layer puts a red dot where each flight ends. The green dots come from scatterplot-start.
This layer draws each flight's path. Click it and change getColor or getWidth.

Try next:
- Click basemap and change zoom under viewState to see more of the coast.
- Click the diamond next to opacity on path-layer, pick a later time in the Timeline, and change it again.
- Press Export and pick Image (PNG) to save the map.
